va_barrow_field.name: Barrow Field
va_barrow_field.desc: A bare hill and two stone doors set into it, facing north. Ivy chokes a loose-looking stone off to one side; the hunter west of the village would know how it moves. The grass here is white, not gray. The wood lies south; a road climbs north toward the moor.

in.lockedMsg: The stone doors are shut fast. If you dropped the seal-stone yourself they will not open again; if not, the priest's blessing, force, or the loose stone will do it.
in.hint: sealed for good if you sealed them; else the blessing, force, or the loose stone

onEnterOnce: So this is where the gray begins. Even the white grass is graying at the edges.

variants.desc: A bare hill and two stone doors, sealed shut again behind you. The grass here is white, not gray, and green is starting to show through it. The wood lies south; a road climbs north toward the moor.
variants.brief: White grass. The doors are sealed, as you left them.

variants.desc: A bare hill and two stone doors standing open into the dark. The grass here is white, not gray, and green is coming through it at last. The wood lies south; a road climbs north toward the moor.
variants.brief: White grass, and green coming through it. The doors stand open.

variants.desc: A bare hill and two stone doors standing open into the dark. The grass here is white, not gray. The wood lies south; a road climbs north toward the moor.
variants.brief: White grass. The stone doors stand open.

actions.label: force the doors — a failed try costs 1hp
fx: Stone grinds on stone. The doors open.
The doors do not move, and the recoil wrenches your shoulder.

actions.label: put your shoulder to the doors (warden)
fx: One good shoulder is all it takes. Stone grinds on stone and gives way at once.

actions.label: work the loose stone by the ivy (wits)
fx: The stone gives when you lean on it; roots and old rain have hollowed a gap beneath. Wedged in the gap, a worn half-token.
The stone shifts and settles back. There is a trick to it you have not found.

actions.label: use the hunter's gap under the stone
fx: Right where the tally said: the stone lifts, and the gap beneath is worn smooth by years of someone's knees. Wedged in it, a worn half-token.

va_antechamber.name: Barrow Antechamber
va_antechamber.desc: Cut stone, cold and faintly echoing. Shelf niches stand empty, robbed bare long before you arrived. A passage north leads to the hall of verses. East, an iron door; down, a crypt that reeks of the same blight fouling the fields.
onEnterOnce: These niches once held tokens for the dead. Someone took them all.

va_vault.name: The King's Strongroom
va_vault.desc: A side chamber the wight never had to guard — the old king trusted iron more than claws. A strongbox sits under years of dust. In the corner a robed shade sits so still you take it for shadow until it speaks. The antechamber lies west.
va_vault.brief: The rusted strongbox. A robed shade.

actions.label: force the strongbox (might)
fx: The rusted lock snaps. Inside: a seal of office, heavy enough to turn a blow, wrapped around a scrap in the king's own hand.
The lock holds. Rust does not mean weak.

actions.label: pick the strongbox's lock (grace)
fx: The old pins give way one by one. Inside: a seal of office, heavy enough to turn a blow, wrapped around a scrap in the king's own hand.
A pin sticks. It can be tried again.

actions.label: ask the shade for the seal (will)
fx: You ask as a steward is asked: plainly, on the king's business. The shade rises, turns a key that was never lost, and sits again. Inside: a seal of office, wrapped around a scrap in the king's own hand.
The shade does not move. 'Iron,' it says, 'or a better reason.'

actions.label: show the shade your worn half-token
fx: The shade stills at the sight of it — the same raised-hand ward it once wore. 'One of ours,' it says, and the rusted lock falls open at a touch. Inside, the king's seal, wrapped around a scrap in his own hand.

va_hall_of_verses.name: Hall of Verses
va_hall_of_verses.desc: Every wall is cut with lines of old writing — the king's verses, meant to be spoken over him. Some of it almost reads itself. The antechamber lies south; a stair climbs to the throne.

up.lockedMsg: There is a stair here somewhere. The walls say where.
up.hint: read the stone verse on these walls first

variants.brief: Walls of old writing. The stair climbs to the throne.

actions.label: read the stone walls (scholar)
fx: 'Let the stone remember what flesh forgets; set it down, and rest.' The verse reads itself to you, plain as speech. Cut beneath it, a stair leads up. Stone verse: known.

actions.label: trace the stone walls by touch (grace)
fx: Quiet fingers find the deep-cut letters. 'Let the stone remember what flesh forgets; set it down, and rest.' Beneath it, a stair. Stone verse: known.
The letters run on past where your fingers can follow. It can be tried again.

actions.label: work out the stone verse (wits)
fx: The verse comes clear. 'Let the stone remember what flesh forgets; set it down, and rest.' Cut beneath it, a stair leads up. Stone verse: known.
The old letters will not hold still. It can be tried again.

va_crypt.name: Barrow Crypt
va_crypt.desc: Low vaults and stone boxes, the air gone sour and the mold black instead of green. Blight-rats scatter between the boxes. A mail shirt is draped over one box. A barrow-wight blocks the north passage, drawn up out of the same rot.

north.lockedMsg: The wight bars the way north. Fight it, slip past it, or go up and around through the hall of verses.
north.hint: defeat it, slip past it (grace), or go around

onEnterOnce: Whoever wore this mail last never got clear of the barrow. The blight pools thickest right here.

variants.brief: Low vaults. The wight is rag and bone.

actions.label: slip past the wight — a fail costs 1hp
fx: You keep to the shadow and slip by. The passage north stands open.
Claws rake you as you dart back.

va_throne.name: Throne of the Barrow
va_throne.desc: The Hollow King sits on a stone seat worn smooth by hands not his own. Where a crown should be, only dust. Cold air gutters your light. South: the crypt. Down: the hall of verses.
onEnterOnce: He does not move against you. Word or blade, whichever ends it, he will let you choose. Kneel to him, though, and you take his place.

variants.name: The Empty Seat
variants.desc: The stone seat is empty. Dust lies in the shape of a man who finally lay down. The air is only cold now, not grieving.

variants.name: The Broken Seat
variants.desc: Dust and old iron on the floor where a king came apart. The stone seat is cracked through.
The Hollow King sits on his stone seat and does not look at you. He has said what he has to say.
variants.brief: The stone seat. He does not look up.

actions.label: weigh what each choice would mean
fx: Rest him — verses, the crown returned or broken — and the great rite stays open. Cut him down: quick, the Regent's answer; that rite is lost. Keep the crown: he grieves on, and a crown can be worn on another seat.

actions.label: speak the three verses over him
fx: You speak the three verses. Relief crosses his face, and he lies down at last. The gray goes out of the air like a tide. Behind you the stone doors wait on your word: seal, or leave open.

actions.label: give back the crown and speak the verses
fx: You set the crown in his hands and speak the three verses over him. He listens with the crown where it belongs, and something settles in his face that four centuries could not. He lies down. The doors await your word.

actions.label: return the crown
fx: You set the crown in his hands. He stands, bows once, and lies down at last. The gray goes out of the trees like a tide. The doors wait on your word.

actions.label: break the crown in front of him
fx: You set the crown on the stone and bring your heel down until the iron gives. He does not move to stop you — you already believed him; that was the debt, more than the metal. He lies down. The doors wait on your word.

actions.label: pocket the crown and leave him grieving
fx: You keep the crown and turn for the stairs, leaving him exactly as you found him. He does not call after you. The gray in the Vale will not lift. Marrowgate will hear that the crown is loose in the world.

actions.label: seal the barrow doors behind you
fx: You draw the great doors shut from within the passage and hear the seal-stone drop. True to your word. The watch will know. The crypt way south still stands open behind you.
You draw the great doors shut and hear the seal-stone drop. You promised no one; you chose it anyway. The priest will grieve the door. The crypt way south still stands open behind you.
Behind the stone, the king you left grieving goes on grieving, unheard now by anyone.

actions.label: leave the barrow open to the sky
fx: You leave the doors as they stand, open to the sky, and your word to the reeve on the barrow floor with them.
You leave the doors open to the sky. Grief needs air, the priest said. You are choosing to believe him.
The king you left grieving keeps his open door and his sky, and the gray with them.

actions.label: (no dawn) kneel and take his place
fx: You lower yourself toward the stone seat and stop, one knee still free. This door does not open back: no verse, no crown, just his place for yours — and no dawn after, for you or the Vale. Kneel again to go through it.

actions.label: (no dawn) finish kneeling
fx: You kneel. The crown of nothing settles on you, light as ash. The Vale will have a king after all, and no dawn.

va_mail_shirt.name: mail shirt
va_mail_shirt.hint: blunts every blow just by riding in your pack

va_kings_seal.name: king's seal
va_kings_seal.hint: read the scrap wrapped around it

fx: 'Forty years I kept faith. It was my own blood who lifted the crown from my sleeping brow and called it inheritance. I do not want the vale to suffer for his theft. I only wanted to be given it back.'

va_keeper_token.name: worn half-token
va_keeper_token.hint: half a ward-sign; the gray priest may know it

fx: A raised hand, snapped off at the wrist. A ward, or half of one. Someone left it at that door on purpose.

va_wight_relic.name: ward-token
va_wight_relic.hint: cold iron worked into a rough sun — hung over a door to keep grief from walking in

va_blight_rats.name: blight rats
onDeath: The rats scatter into the dark between the boxes.

va_barrow_wight.name: barrow-wight
onDeath: The wight comes apart into rag and bone. Among the scraps, a ward-token of cold iron, the kind hung over a door to keep grief from walking in.

topics.label: who kept this room
topics.say: Forty years I held this key, and the king's trust with it. I do not haunt the box — only what it meant, that a man's word once needed iron behind it to be believed.

topics.label: the seal you kept
topics.say: His own blood pried the crown loose that same week — I heard both locks give, his and mine, one after the other. I kept faith with the wrong door.

va_hollow_king.name: hollow king
va_hollow_king.desc: A king the shape of grief, sitting very still.
onDeath: Your blade finds him and he breaks apart into dust and old iron, a king who never got his crown back. The blight thins with him. It does not lift. The doors wait on your word.

topics.label: why do you grieve
topics.say: My crown. The first reeve took it from my barrow, and my rest went with it. Bring it back, or speak the old verses over me — either rests me; both together rests me deeper. Kneel, and my seat and my grief are yours.

topics.label: the blight
topics.say: It is my grief, spilled over the land. It will not stop while I wake. And I am not the only one awake in this Reach. Ask the living what they have let lapse.

topics.label: the first reeve
topics.say: He was my own blood, and the vale was starving, and a crown buys grain. He did not take it out of malice. His line rules in Marrowgate now, on what he took. They have never once come to say so.

topics.label: do you forgive him
topics.say: I do not curse his name, whatever the vale calls him for it. If I begrudge anything, it is that he never came back to tell me why. A grief told is half a grief. That is what the verses are for.

topics.label: the barrow doors — seal or open?
topics.say: Sealed or open, it is no longer mine to keep. The reeve fears what walks free; the priest fears a shut door on grief undone. Both are half right. Leave it however you see fit.

topics.label: you may soon rest
topics.say: Three. Water for grief my own hands could not lay down, wind for what iron never carried off, stone for what my flesh forgot. Say them, when you are ready.

topics.label: step back from the seat
topics.say: I have waited four hundred years. I can wait while you decide.

stages.text: The king is settled. The doors are yours to seal or leave open, from the throne.
You promised the reeve to seal the barrow once the king rests: a door shut on the dead, the priest would say.
The reeve wants the barrow sealed after; the priest wants it open. Promise, or don't — you decide at the throne.
All three verses are yours. Speak them over the king at the throne.
Stone and wind are yours. One verse left: the sunken shrine, in the wood east of the village.
Stone and water are yours. One verse left: the old watchtower, east of the wood.
Water and wind are yours. One verse left: the barrow's own hall.
Stone verse known. Two more: the sunken shrine and the old watchtower, both east of the wood.
Water verse known. Two more: the old watchtower, east of the wood, and the barrow's own hall.
Wind verse known. Two more: the sunken shrine, east of the wood, and the barrow's own hall.
Three verses were cut for the king: the sunken shrine and the old watchtower east of the wood, and the barrow's hall.
The crown is yours. Return it to the king at the throne — or decide otherwise.
You have heard the king's grief. Press it on the elder, or bring her the king's seal from the barrow's strongroom.
The elder keeps the crown in a locked coffer, and will not open it until you have heard the king grieve himself.

epilogue.text: Of the Hollow King the Vale says only that he sleeps, crowned, and that the grass on his hill is the greenest in the Reach.
The reeve of Last Light kept the watch shield you gave back, and never spoke your name again.
No wolves run the Ashwood now. The hunter says the wood is quieter for it, and does not say whether that is good.
The reeve of Last Light never got his watch shield back, nor a word of why, and never spoke your name again.
